line: It was not necessary to abduct us.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I am sorry, but after speaking with Ro Laren, I decided that it was.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Then she has done us both a disservice. I am committed to peace.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I am not at all interested in peace. And I am not convinced you are, either.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Captain, I did not come here to undermine this mission.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Whatever your motives, you've already done enough to damage these negotiations.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I came here to convince these people to listen to you. I didn't want this to end in bloodshed.

title: Ensign Ro
line: There will be no bloodshed.

title: Ensign Ro
line: You don't know all the facts, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Then perhaps you would share them with me, Ensign.

title: Ensign Ro
line: All is not what it seems to be, Captain. Perhaps someone is using you to get to me. Perhaps you are a victim of this deception as well. I do not know.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Deception?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Your mission was to seek out the Bajoran terrorists who destroyed the Federation settlement on Solarion Four.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Yes.

title: Ensign Ro
line: As I have informed Ro Laren, it was not the Bajora.

title: Ensign Ro
line: He admits responsibility for dozens of attacks on Cardassian targets. Why should we believe him about Solarion Four?

title: Ensign Ro
line: He has no reason to lie.

title: Ensign Ro
line: He fears our reprisal.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I perceived no fear or deception from him.

title: Ensign Ro
line: If they did not attack Solarion Four, then who did? And why would anyone want to falsely implicate the Bajora?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Perhaps someone wanted to draw us into the conflict.

title: Ensign Ro
line: What would anyone gain by doing that?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign Ro, may I see you in my Ready room?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Yes, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: You do not leave this ship without authorisation.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Captain, I'm sorry, but I

title: Ensign Ro
line: This is not a discussion. You're restricted to your quarters for the remainder of this mission. Dismissed.

title: Ensign Ro
line: What?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Hello, it's me, Guinan. I heard you got grounded.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I really don't feel like talking right now.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Come on, sure you do.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Why is it, every time I tell you something, you tell me I mean the exact opposite?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Because you're one of those people who's got their poles reversed. Do you want to talk about it?

title: Ensign Ro
line: It's nothing you can help me with.

title: Ensign Ro
line: How do you know until you try?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Look, I got myself into this. I'm just trying to figure a way out. That's all. Without anyone getting killed this time. Seems like everybody's just pulling my strings, you know? Like I've got no control.

title: Ensign Ro
line: For people like you and me, who've lost their homes, sometimes that's the way life feels.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I'm in trouble. There's more going on here than anybody on this ship realizes. It's more than I know how to deal with. And I really don't know who to trust anymore.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Including yourself?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Especially myself.

title: Ensign Ro
line: You know, a very long time ago, I got into some serious trouble too. And I mean serious. And I'd probably still be there if I hadn't trusted one man.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Come.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign Ro has some things she'd like to talk to you about.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign Ro has been confined to her quarters.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Well, she can go back to her quarters when she's done.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Guinan, I don't know why you are involved in this, but

title: Ensign Ro
line: She's my friend.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Please sit down. Guinan is very selective about whom she calls a friend.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Sir, when I'm finished telling you what I have to tell you, I'm probably going to end up back in the stockade one way or the other. And if that's how this has to be, then I just can't do this anymore.

title: Ensign Ro
line: What can you not do anymore, Ensign?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Admiral Kennelly came to me in prison and told me he'd arrange to get me out if I'd go on a mission.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I know that part.

title: Ensign Ro
line: No, sir. Not this mission. One for him and only him. You were being sent to talk, to negotiate. The Admiral knew that was hopeless. My job was to give Orta an incentive.

title: Ensign Ro
line: What kind of incentive?

title: Ensign Ro
line: One that you couldn't offer. One that Starfleet couldn't offer. Orta was to end the terrorism against the Federation and return with his people to the camps. In exchange he would get weapons, ships, things that would really make a difference against the Cardassians in the future.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I find that almost impossible to believe. That Admiral Kennelly would consider supplying weapons to the terrorists?

title: Ensign Ro
line: If you ask him, he'll deny it. But it's true. I didn't leave the ship without authorisation, Captain. I received it from the Admiral last night.

title: Ensign Ro
line: You have been in contact with Admiral Kennelly during this mission?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Yes, sir. The subspace log can confirm that part of it at least.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Arming these people is a violation of everything that the Federation stands for. Even you cannot be blind to that.

title: Ensign Ro
line: No, sir, I'm not. But this was something I had to do. You see, Captain, when I was seven years old I was given a piece of sugar candy and I was led by a Cardassian into a room where my father was sitting. And he looked at me with eyes I'd never seen. The Cardassian began to ask him questions, and during the next two hours, as I was forced to watch, my father was tortured until he died. And I remember feeling so ashamed of him as he begged for mercy. I was ashamed of him for being weak. I was ashamed of being Bajoran. Later I began to understand how misguided those feelings were. And yet somehow, they have remained a part of me. I don't want to be ashamed of my heritage any longer, Captain. I serve the Federation. But I am Bajoran. A Starfleet Admiral presented me with an opportunity to help my people in their fight against the Cardassians. I had to accept it.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Have you made this offer to Orta?

title: Ensign Ro
line: No. After he told me the Bajora hadn't attacked Solarion Four, nothing made sense anymore. I decided to wait until I could figure out what was going on.

title: Ensign Ro
line: That was a wise choice, Ensign. It probably saved you from another court martial. Have you briefed Admiral Kennelly since we returned from the surface?

title: Ensign Ro
line: No, sir. Captain, I don't know who to trust anymore. But that strange bartender of yours has a way of getting to you, and she said that you were her friend.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Then we have one thing in common. Do you think that Orta would cooperate with us to determine the truth here?

title: Ensign Ro
line: I think I could persuade him to.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Good. Our orders were to find him, to bring him back to the camps any way we could. Perhaps that is exactly what we should do.

title: Ensign Ro
line: And then what?

title: Ensign Ro
line: And then watch what happens.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Captain's log, supplemental. I have become convinced that we are somehow involved in a conspiracy. I am hopeful the purpose behind it will be revealed in the next few hours.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Well done, Captain.

title: Ensign Ro
line: It was a team effort, Admiral. Ensign Ro was invaluable.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Good. What's the next step?

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Enterprise will escort a Bajoran Antares class carrier to the Valo Three camp at oh five hundred hours. Orta and his people will be aboard.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Good. Keep us advised of your progress.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Acknowledged. How's that Cardassian virus, Admiral?

title: Ensign Ro
line: A lot better, thank you.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I'm pleased. We will report as soon as our mission is accomplished. Picard out.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign Ro, take us to the designated coordinates.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Aye, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Mister Data, keep an eye on the Cardassian border.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Aye, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Bajoran vessel is moving up from the surface, Captain.

title: Ensign Ro
line: On screen. Hail them, Mister Worf.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Audio channel open. The ship does not have visual capabilities.

title: Ensign Ro
line: This is Captain Picard. We're prepared to escort you to Valo Three.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Acknowledged, Captain. Be advised that our ship is limited to half impulse.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign Ro, set a course for Valo Three, half impulse.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Aye, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I am monitoring increased activity inside Cardassian space. Two ships are moving along the border heading one four two mark zero five one.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Can you identify the class of these ships, Mister Worf?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Cardassian warships, Galor class, type three.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Top of the line.

title: Ensign Ro
line: They are moving into a course parallel to our own, Captain.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Yellow alert. Continue to monitor them.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign Ro, what's the closest we come to the Cardassian border on our current heading to Valo Three?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Thirteen thousand, four hundred kilometers, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: ETA?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Eight minutes.

title: Ensign Ro
line: That's where it will be.

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Cardassian ships are changing course, sir. They are crossing the border.

title: Ensign Ro
line: They're increasing power to their forward weapon grid.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Red alert.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign Ro, set a course to intercept the Cardassians. Mister Worf, open a channel to the Bajoran vessel.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Open.

title: Ensign Ro
line: This is the Enterprise. We are moving to intercept two Cardassian warships. Maintain your present course and speed.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Acknowledged, Enterprise.

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Cardassians are within visual range.

title: Ensign Ro
line: On screen.

title: Ensign Ro
line: They are hailing us, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Open a channel, Mister Worf. This is Captain Jean-Luc Picard of the Federation Starship Enterprise. How can we help you?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Gul Dolak, Cardassian Militia Four One. We have no argument with you, Captain.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I'm pleased to hear that, Gul Dolak, for all of us in the Federation value the peaceful relations with our Cardassian neighbors.

title: Ensign Ro
line: No more than we value the relations with our Federation neighbors.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Well, now that we've established our mutual good will, what's on your mind?

title: Ensign Ro
line: We have identified the Bajoran ship you are escorting as a terrorist carrier.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Terrorist carrier? Are you certain?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Most certain, Captain. It has committed many crimes against us. We know its markings well.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Rest assured, Gul Dolak, there will be no terrorist attacks today. We are escorting the Bajoran settlers to their camp on Valo Three. You can monitor their course if you wish.

title: Ensign Ro
line: We would request that you withdraw and leave the matter to us.

title: Ensign Ro
line: This is neutral space, Gul Dolak. You have no jurisdiction here.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Nor do you.

title: Ensign Ro
line: If we withdraw, what do you intend to do with the Bajoran vessel?

title: Ensign Ro
line: We intend to destroy it.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I see. That puts me in a difficult position. I promised to escort these people to their camps.

title: Ensign Ro
line: You are protecting the enemies of the Cardassian people. If you do not withdraw, we will take great offense.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I'm sorry to offend you, Gul Dolak, but we cannot withdraw.

title: Ensign Ro
line: We are prepared to take any steps necessary.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Is that intended as a threat?

title: Ensign Ro
line: It is a complaint from your Cardassian neighbors. You have one hour to withdraw.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Advise Starfleet of our status, Mister Data. When Admiral Kennelly calls, I'll speak to him in my Ready room.

title: Ensign Ro
line: It seemed, Admiral, that they knew our course, our destination, our plan.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I'm sure they monitor the border at all times for terrorist activity. Their sensors must picked up Orta's ship, that's all.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I'm not convinced of that.

title: Ensign Ro
line: The important thing is, what do we do now?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Do you have any suggestions, Admiral?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Your top priority is to protect the Cardassian treaty.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Sir, I see no way to protect the Cardassian peace without sacrificing the Bajorans.

title: Ensign Ro
line: If that's your call, I'll support it.

title: Ensign Ro
line: No. I'm not willing to give them up.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I don't think you're looking at the big picture, Jean-Luc. We can't afford to lose the Cardassian treaty.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Well, I just see a different big picture, Admiral. It looks something like this. I see the Cardassian liaison, with his Cardassian virus, coming to meet with you after the attack on Solarion Four. Now we have a common enemy, he says. The Bajoran terrorists. The Cardassians can't find them, but maybe the Federation can. I'm beginning to see that our mission has, in fact, been to expose Orta so that the Cardassians can move in and destroy him.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I think you've lost your perspective, Captain. We'll discuss this further when you return. For now, I'm giving you a direct order to withdraw. Kennelly out.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign Ro, set a course, bearing one eight seven mark one zero two, one quarter impulse.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Aye, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: He's ordered us to withdraw?

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Cardassians are moving toward the Bajoran vessel, Captain.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Hold present course.

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Bajoran ship has been destroyed.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Subspace signal coming from Starfleet, Captain. Admiral Kennelly.

title: Ensign Ro
line: On screen.

title: Ensign Ro
line: It is on a secure channel, sir. In your ready room?

title: Ensign Ro
line: No. Here. On screen.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Report.

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Cardassians have destroyed the Bajoran ship, Admiral.

title: Ensign Ro
line: All hands lost?

title: Ensign Ro
line: No, sir.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Survivors?

title: Ensign Ro
line: No, sir. No one was on board.

title: Ensign Ro
line: What are you talking about?

title: Ensign Ro
line: The ship was controlled from the ground. Communication was handled through a subspace relay on board the vessel.

title: Ensign Ro
line: This was your idea, Picard?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Actually, no. It was Ensign Ro's idea but I fully endorsed it. I suspected that something like this might occur.

title: Ensign Ro
line: They're terrorists, damn it. Why in the hell would you want to protect them?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Admiral, I am more concerned with protecting the honor and integrity of Starfleet.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Do you know how many of our people they killed on Solarion Four?

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Bajorans did not attack Solarion Four.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Who told you that? Orta?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Yes.

title: Ensign Ro
line: And you believed him?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Admiral, Orta's ships are old and obsolete. They don't even have warp capabilities. They couldn't have reached another star system, let alone attacked one.

title: Ensign Ro
line: But then who's responsible?

title: Ensign Ro
line: I would suggest you ask your friend the Cardassian liaison, Admiral. The only explanation I can think of is that the Cardassians staged it.

title: Ensign Ro
line: The Cardassians? Why?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Perhaps they were hoping to find someone in Starfleet like you, Admiral, naive enough to solve their Bajoran problem for them.

title: Ensign Ro
line: What will happen to him?

title: Ensign Ro
line: I'm not sure. A hearing, certainly. Probably a court martial.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Well, if he's sent to the stockade on Jaros Two, tell him to request a room in the east wing. The west wing gets awfully hot in the afternoons. How soon do you intend to return to Lya Station Alpha, sir?

title: Ensign Ro
line: In a few weeks. We have some surveying to do in sector two one three oh five.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Perhaps I should arrange for some other transportation back.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Ensign, you were recruited for one mission and if you wish to be relieved of further duty, I can certainly arrange it. But I'd like you to consider remaining in Starfleet.

title: Ensign Ro
line: You're not serious.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I think it would be a shame for Starfleet to lose someone of your potential.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Well, thank you, Captain, but this uniform just doesn't fit, and you know it.

title: Ensign Ro
line: That can change.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I don't think so.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I've noticed qualities in you that could be harnessed, molded.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Don't count on it.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I think you've got a great deal to learn from Starfleet.

title: Ensign Ro
line: I always thought Starfleet had a lot to learn from me, Captain.

title: Ensign Ro
line: That is an attitude I've found common among the best officers I've ever served with. You're not one of them yet, but you could be, if you work at it.

title: Ensign Ro
line: That's an interesting challenge. And I rarely refuse an interesting challenge. There would have to be one condition.

title: Ensign Ro
line: Condition?

title: Ensign Ro
line: Picard to Enterprise. Two to beam up.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: The hospital facility will be located there, facing north in that grove of trees. And the school and the arts center will be standing there, centrally located among the residential pods.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Very good. At this rate we'll be able to bring the next wave of colonists in in about six months. I've to tell you I envy you. This is a beautiful place to put down roots.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Somehow, Riker, you don't strike me as the kind that puts down roots.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: No? How do I strike you?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: As a free spirit. An adventurer.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: An adventurer? Aren't you pioneers adventurers at heart?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Of course. But we also have this nesting instinct. It's exciting to find a new world but the joy comes in making it a home. Building houses, having children.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Very interesting. I'd love to discuss this further with you. Dinner tonight?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: If you want to share camp rations in my tent, I'd be delighted.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Haven't we gotten you a replicator yet?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: No, we haven't, but I've been saving my ration of dried chicken curry. It should go very nicely with that bottle of wine I happen to know you brought with you.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: This is sounding better all the time.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: And as you know, I provide the most memorable desserts.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: My favorite part of dinner.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Will? Carmen? We've been going over the schematics for the hospital. The location seems fine.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: When the Enterprise comes back tomorrow, we'll get a crew started on that.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Carmen, have you got construction started I didn't know about?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: No. What is that?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Data?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I do not recognize the sound. I believe it is coming from above.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Will, what is it?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Data, what's our best bet for cover?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Subterranean caverns to the east, sir. Doctor.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Will.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Start gathering everybody together. We've seen this before. We know what it is. Now get moving.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Follow him. Let's go! Come on, come on!

title: Silicon Avatar
line: No, stay together! Stay together! This way! This way! This way!

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I've got you.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Will, help us!

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Data! Carmen!

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Captain, sensors indicate a disturbance near the outpost on Melona Four.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: What kind of disturbance?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I cannot tell. We are still too far away. It could be an electrical storm.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: See if you can contact the colony.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Aye, sir. Captain, there is no response from Melona colony, but the disturbance in the atmosphere is increasing.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: How far are we?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: At current speed, twenty seven hours.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Bridge to La Forge.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: La Forge here, Captain.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Are you picking up any readings from Melona?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Yes, sir. Something strange is going on. There are violent disruptions in the atmosphere.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Ensign, increase to warp eight.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Come on, keep moving.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Watch your step but keep moving.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Let's go, let's go. Keep moving. Deeper into the cave. Come on. Deeper into the cave. Keep moving.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: How much protection will this cave give us?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: The refractory metal in the rock formations may act as an effective barrier.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Let's seal off this entrance.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Let's hope there's enough air in here.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: There's got to be a ventilation source somewhere. We need some light.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: How are the others?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Just scrapes and bruises, I think. I'll check further. Where's Carmen?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: She didn't make it. She was trying to save an old man who'd fallen.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I'm sorry.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I think we're going to be all right in here. I'm not sure about the air supply, so stay put, don't move around. Don't expend unnecessary energy. With any luck, we'll be able to wait this thing out.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Riker to Enterprise. Riker to Enterprise.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Commander, the refractory metals in the rock strata may also interfere with communication.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Data we've only seen the Crystalline Entity once before. How do you know these metals will protect us?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I am not entirely certain they will, sir.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I was afraid you were going to say something like that.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Sir, the disturbance on Melona is becoming more intense.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Keep hailing them. All channels, Mister Worf.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Captain, the fact that they're not responding doesn't necessarily mean there's anything wrong. The atmospheric disturbance could be jamming the signal.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I know, Counselor.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Still no response, sir.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Increase to warp nine. How long, Mister Worf?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Six hours.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I've got one man unconscious. We can't stay in here much longer.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: If I open that entrance and it's still out there, we're dead.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: If we all stay in here, we're dead.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: It has been over an hour since we heard the Entity, sir. It may be gone.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Or it may be out there waiting for us.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Everybody stay here.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Commander? Commander Riker, are you there?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Lieutenant Worf, I don't think I've ever seen a more beautiful sight.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: It's good to see you're all right, Commander. What's happened here?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: The Crystalline Entity paid us a visit. We lost two colonists, but we got the rest in here.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Captain's log, stardate 45122.3. We have notified Starfleet Command of our intention to pursue and investigate the Crystalline Entity. To that end, we have been joined by Doctor Kila Marr, a xenologist who has made studying the Entity her life's work.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Welcome to the Enterprise. I am Commander William Riker.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Commander, Doctor Kila Marr.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Glad you're here.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: You were on the surface during the attack?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: That's right.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Remarkable. You and your group are the only known beings ever to survive an assault by the Crystalline Entity.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: We were lucky.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I should say. And your android. He was there, too?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Lieutenant Commander Data was there, yes.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Well, shall we get started?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I'd be glad to show you to your quarters.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Oh, Commander. A chance to talk to survivors so soon after an attack? I've been waiting years for this. I don't want to waste a moment more.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: And when we came out of the cave there was nothing left. Everywhere we looked there was complete devastation. Trees gone, nothing.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: That's typical. It could take years for anything to grow again.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Doctor, I ran a full spectrographic analysis, section by section. Trace elements confirm that it is the same entity which destroyed the colony at Omicron Theta.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: The Crystalline Entity seems to function like a gigantic electromagnetic collector. It needs a lot of power to keep going so it strips every form of life from the worlds it encounters and converts it all into energy.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: There's no vegetation, no insects, not even soil bacteria. It left nothing.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Except witnesses, for the first time in eleven recorded attacks. Now why, I wonder, did it spare your group?

title: Silicon Avatar
line: It didn't spare everyone, Doctor. If you'll check your reports, you'll find that two of the colonists didn't survive.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: My point is that until now there have never been any survivors.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Doctor, the cave in which we hid was made of rock which contained heavy concentrations of kelbonite and fistrium. We surmise that the Entity was unable to penetrate that barrier.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: I would like to do interviews with each of the survivors. Collect as much specific detail as I can of their observations.

title: Silicon Avatar
line: Of course.

title: Silicon Avatar

title: Unification Part Two
line: That is not satisfactory.

title: Unification Part Two
line: You cannot remain here, Captain Picard.

title: Unification Part Two
line: And I will not return without a full explanation. Ambassador, with great respect for all that you've achieved on behalf of the Federation, this sort of cowboy diplomacy will not easily be tolerated any more.

title: Unification Part Two
line: Cowboy diplomacy?

title: Unification Part Two
line: If you wish to undertake a mission with obvious repercussions to the Federation, then you should discuss it with the Federation. I'm here as their representative. You'll have to discuss it with me.

title: Unification Part Two

title: Unification Part Two
line: I also have the responsibility of being the bearer of unhappy news.

title: Unification Part Two
line: Sarek? Sarek is dead? Walk with me, Picard.

title: Unification Part Two
line: I know of your mind-meld with my father which enabled him to complete his last mission.

title: Unification Part Two
line: It was an honor. He is a great man.

title: Unification Part Two
line: He was a great representative of the Vulcan people and of the Federation.

title: Unification Part Two
line: I was with him before coming here. He expressed his pride in you. His love.

title: Unification Part Two
line: Emotional disarray was a symptom of the illness from which he suffered.

title: Unification Part Two
line: No, those feelings came from his heart, Spock. He shared them with me. I know.

title: Unification Part Two
line: Sarek would no more approve my coming here than you do, Picard. For some time now, I've been aware of a growing movement here of people who seek to learn the ideals of the Vulcan philosophy. He asked me to come now, because he believes it may be time to take the first step toward reunification.

title: Unification Part Two
line: Reunification? After so many centuries? After so many fundamental differences have evolved between your peoples?

title: Unification Part Two
line: It would seem unlikely to succeed, but I cannot ignore the potential rewards that a union between our two worlds would bring.

title: Unification Part Two
line: What is this first step that Pardek suggests?

line: There is a new Proconsul in the Romulan Senate. He is young and idealistic. He has promised many reforms. Pardek believes that he may be receptive to discussing reunification.

title: Unification Part Two
line: Why would you not bring something so important to the attention of your own people or the Federation?

title: Unification Part Two
line: A personal decision, Captain. Perhaps you are aware of the small role I played in the overture to peace with the Klingons.

title: Unification Part Two
line: History is aware of the role you played, Ambassador.

title: Unification Part Two
line: Not entirely. It was I who committed Captain Kirk to that peace mission, and I who had to bear the responsibility for the consequences to him and his crew. Quite simply, I am unwilling to risk anyone's life but my own on this occasion. So I ask you respect my wishes and leave.

title: Unification Part Two
line: Ambassador, your logic escapes me. If I didn't know better, I would say that your judgment is influenced by your emotions.

title: Unification Part Two

line: Leave the holodeck? No, of course not. You can only exist in here.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Damn you, Picard. He promised me something would be done. I should have realized he would have said anything to get me to release my hostage.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Hostage?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: How long have I been locked away?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, it l ooks like about four years.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: It seemed longer.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: What are you talking about? You can't possibly have been aware of the passage of time.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: But I was. Brief, terrifying periods of consciousness. Disembodied. Without substance.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I don't see how that could be possible. Maybe there was a fragmentation of the protected memory circuits.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Call it what you will. All I know is that despite Picard's promise, he's done nothing. Just left me to go quietly mad.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: He would not have forgotten his promise. The Captain would not do that.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I'd like to talk to him.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, I can ask.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Ask him to meet me in the sitting room at Baker Street. That would be far more appropriate.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I'll have to store you in memory again until I get an answer.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Captain's log, stardate 46424.1. The Enterprise has arrived at the Detrian system to observe a unique celestial event the collision of two planets.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Since both planets are gas giants, neither possesses a solid surface. Their atmospheres, however, will come into contact in approximately seventeen hours nine minutes.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: If their collision causes a self-sustaining fusion reaction, this is what we are likely to see. The birth of a new star. The Enterprise will hold position until the gravitational instability subsides and we can get in for a closer look. Now I want triple redundancy on all of the sensor arrays. We'll probably never get another chance to see something like this. I don't want to miss anything. Okay?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Commander, you'll never believe what happened while I was working on your program in the holodeck. Professor Moriarty appeared, out of nowhere.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: What?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: And he wants to talk to the Captain.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Computer, begin Sherlock Holmes program three A and place us in the drawing room at Two Twenty One B Baker Street.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Program complete.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Computer, access protected memory and run Moriarty program.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor. It's good to see you again.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: If you'd missed my company, I should think you'd have summoned me before now.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I want to assure you that we've not forgotten you. We spent some time investigating how you became self-aware. Frankly, it still remains a mystery.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: It is also irrelevant. What concerns me is finding a way to leave the holodeck.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: We have been wrestling with that problem too, unfortunately without any success. But we have turned our findings over to Starfleet's most experienced theoretical scientists.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: And what did your finest minds come up with?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Unfortunately, they have not arrived at a solution either.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I see.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, I am concerned to learn that you experienced the passage of time while you were stored in the computer memory. I can assure you, we had no idea that that would be the case.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Enough of this. I no longer believe anything you say.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, I understand your frustration.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Do you really? When this is over, you will walk out of this room to the real world and your own concerns, and leave me here trapped in a world I know to be nothing but illusion. I cannot bear that. I must leave.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: That is not possible. You cannot exist outside this room.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Are you certain of that?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Computer, exit.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Although an object appears solid on the holodeck, in the real world they have no substance.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: An object has no life. I do.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, you are a computer simulation.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I have consciousness. Conscious beings have will. The mind endows them with powers that are not necessarily understood, even by you. If my will is strong enough, perhaps I can exist outside this room. Perhaps I can walk into your world right now.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, I ask you to believe me. If you step out of that door, you will cease to exist.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: If I am nothing more than a computer simulation, then very little will have been lost. But if I am right? Mind over matter. Cogito ergo sum.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I think therefore I am.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Data to Security. Send two officers to holodeck three.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: How is this possible?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: It isn't.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: This contradicts everything we know about holodeck physics.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Then perhaps you don't know as much as you thought.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, will you come with me? I'd like our Doctor to examine you.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Certainly, sir. Policemen. I'd recognize them in any century.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: As far as I can tell, he's real. He's human.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: What else would I be, dear lady?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: His DNA is a little unusual, but all the major systems are there and functioning normally.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: As far as I can tell there's no evidence that his molecules are losing any cohesion. They seem to be as immutable as ordinary matter.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, Professor, my crew will continue to investigate, but for now it would seem you have accomplished a miracle. The question is, now that you're here, what do we do with you?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I ask only that I be allowed to explore this new world. Your vessel, for instance. What sea does she sail? Might we go above deck? Weather permitting, of course.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, I think there are some things of which you should be made aware.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: My God! We're adrift in the heavens.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: No, not adrift. The Enterprise is a starship, capable of traveling through space.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Extraordinary. Are we far from Earth? What is the range of this ship? What means of locomotion does it use? There's so much for me to learn. I hardly know where to start.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I can give you books that will help.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Good, good. I want to start making plans. Determine what I'm going to do with my life.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I hope you will plan on remaining on board for a while. There is still much that we need to understand about what has happened to you.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Does it really matter? The point is, I'm here, and I'm eager to get on with life.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, I feel it necessary to point out that criminal behavior is as unacceptable in the twenty fourth century as it was in the nineteenth. And much harder to get away with.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Don't worry, Captain. My past is nothing but a fiction. The scribblings of an Englishman dead now for four centuries. I hope to leave his books on the shelf, as it were.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: If that's so, then there are opportunities awaiting you that are beyond anything you have ever imagined.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Your century may welcome me, but

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: What is the matter?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: In considering all these vast possibilities, I suddenly feel very much alone. I am a man out of time, Captain, and that isolates me. You have been more gracious than I could ever have imagined, I wonder, may I impose on your generosity once again? There is a woman, the Countess Regina Bartholomew. She was created as a holodeck character for one of Commander Data's programs. She was designed to be the love of my life. Could she also be brought off the holodeck?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, I ask you to believe me when I say that we do not know how or why you are able to exist off the holodeck.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I do. I do believe you.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: According to the laws of physics, this is impossible. We would have no idea how to do it again.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: As I understand it, I was endowed with consciousness four years ago when someone said to the computer, create an opponent with a capacity to out-think Data. or words to that effect. Could we not make a similar request on behalf of the Countess?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Even if I had reason to believe that would be successful, I don't think that I could sanction it. Please understand, Professor, that you are in essence a new life form. One that we didn't intend to create and that we don't fully understand. Now the moral and ethical implications of deliberately creating another one like you are overwhelming.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Is it morally and ethically acceptable to deny the woman I love so that you can put your conscience at ease? Are you saying that you will simply dictate how I am to live my life?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I assure you, we will do everything possible to make you comfortable.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: So long as I accept the terms under which you dole out those comforts. Captain, I am a powerless man. You hold my future, my happiness, my very life in your hands. Please, consider my request.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I understand his frustration. We created him and we created her to be the woman he loves. Surely we have some responsibility to them.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: It's very romantic, but until we know just what it was that walked off the holodeck, I don't think we should be trying it again.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Even if we decided to do it, there's no guarantee that we'd be able to.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: There is also no way of knowing if the Professor's ability to exist off the holodeck is permanent. It may be unwise to consider creating a second individual while this uncertainty exists.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Agreed. We don't have enough information about this phenomenon to act in a responsible way. I think we'll hold off on Professor Moriarty's request for now, but continue with your investigation. In the meantime, I have to deal with Professor Moriarty.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I feel I must postpone action until we learn more.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Yes. You know all about that. I stayed in the dungeon of your computer for years waiting for you to learn more. It wasn't until I took things into my own hands that something got done.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, I wonder why you're in so much of a hurry. Is this woman involved with you in some illegal venture?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Your computer designed her to be a person of impeccable integrity. She would never commit a crime.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: You must love her very much.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: The program fashioned her for me to love. But I must admit, I would have done so anyway. She is remarkable. My life has not been the same since I met her. I don't simply love her, Captain. I adore her.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Then her safety must be very important to you. Give us time to determine what is going on happened here. That way we can minimize the risks in bringing her to you. You wouldn't want to lose her because we acted too quickly.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Riker to Captain Picard.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Picard here.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Could you join us on the Bridge?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: On my way.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: There they are, Captain.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: How long until they begin to coalesce?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Within the next five hours, sir.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Mister Worf, launch four Class A probes toward the planets.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Aye, sir.

line: Mister Worf?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I don't understand.

line: Controls are not responding.

line: For what reason?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Unknown, sir.

line: Computer, route all command functions to the Bridge.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Explain.

line: Picard command codes are no longer valid.

line: What's happening? Who's transferred the voice authorisation?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I have. I'm afraid I had no choice but to take control of your vessel.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: If you harm me, sir, I will not be able to relinquish voice control of your vessel.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Professor, this situation is more serious than you realize. In less than five hours, those two planets will collide and a new star will form. Unless we move to a safe distance, this vessel will be destroyed.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I'm just a fictional character. I haven't much to lose.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: But surely you wish to live like the rest of us?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Not alone. Not without the Countess.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: We've discussed that. We are studying means of bringing her safely off the holodeck. But five hours is not enough time.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I'm not so sure. A deadline has a wonderful way of concentrating the mind.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Mister Data, will you investigate the possibility of complying with Professor Moriarty's request.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Aye, sir.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: In the meantime, we have a few things to discuss.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Perhaps we should consider the transporter system. It uses many of the same principles as the holodeck. Both, for example, are capable of converting energy into matter.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Except the transporter reconstitutes energy in a permanent form. Holodeck matter doesn't have any cohesion unless it's inside the grid.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I wonder, what would happen if we tried to beam a holodeck object off the grid?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Nothing would happen. A holodeck object is just a simulation. There's nothing there to provide a pattern lock for the transporter.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: However, if it were possible to lock onto the object, it might rematerialize with the same molecular cohesion as conventional matter.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: That's a big leap, Data. I just don't think the transporter is going to accept simulated matter.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Unless, unless we could find a way to compensate for the phase variance. If we could modify the pattern enhancers we just might do it.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, Professor Moriarty has agreed not to interfere with routine ship operations so long as he believes we're acting in good faith, then I don't think we're in immediate danger. Any progress?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: We were just talking about using the transporter to beam the Countess off the holodeck, but I don't quite see how it's going to work.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, keep at it. I have to tell him that we are making some progress. Mister La Forge. Do you have any idea how Moriarty could have gained control of the ship?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Somehow he managed to override the security lockouts and rewrite them. The man is brilliant in any century.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I want you to find some way to undo what he has done so that we can regain control of this ship.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Set the pattern enhancers around whatever object you wish to transport. I will proceed to the transporter room and begin modifications.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Computer, run Sherlock Holmes Program three A.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: That program is already in use.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Are you here to see Mister Holmes, or perhaps Professor Moriarty? Neither is in just now.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Um, er, no. No, no. I'm not here to see anyone. I'm just here to deliver these.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Fine. Just put them anywhere.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Actually, I have to put them right here.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: How curious. Why is that?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, it has to do with, er, it's nothing you need to worry about, Countess.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Are you suggesting that it's beyond my comprehension?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: It's really very simple. I need to enhance the molecular pattern of this chair so that the transporter can get a better lock on the signal.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: This has to do with taking James and me into the real world.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: You, you, you know about that? You understand about the real world?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: James has explained it to me. It sounds like a grand adventure. There's nothing I love more than voyaging in the unknown. Have you ever been to Africa, Mister?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Er, Barclay. Lieutenant Reginald Barclay. No, no, I haven't.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I have. When I was seventeen I went on safari with my uncle. My mother took to her bed in terror I'd be bitten by tsetse fly, but I had a marvelous time. I got to wear trousers the whole time. It was hard to go back to a corset, I can tell you.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Yes, I'm sure it was.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: After that, I never stopped traveling. I couldn't bear to be stuck in one place for very long. So you see I'm so looking forward to this new experience. My. Traveling the stars.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: You know about that? You know where we are? Countess, forgive me, but you just don't sound like a holodeck character.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: That's because she isn't.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: James!

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: If you loved a woman like this, Lieutenant, would you be content to let her remain a simulation?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: You, you gave her consciousness?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Yes, just as it was given to me.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well I'm not so sure that's a good idea.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Nonsense. It was the only thing to do.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Have you tried to take her off the holodeck yet?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: No. I am unwilling to risk the Countess' safety. I want to make sure nothing will happen to her.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: We may be closer to freedom than you think, James. These devices will enhance our molecular patterns. They'll help take us into the real world.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Oh, please, proceed.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, we're going to try to transport this chair off the holodeck first. We didn't want to try it on the Countess until we were sure it would work.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: How thoughtful. Isn't he thoughtful, James?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Barclay to Commander Data.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Go ahead, Lieutenant.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I'm ready here.

line: Modifications are complete.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Stand by.

line: Standing by.

line: Activating pattern enhancers. Energizing. I am having difficulty establishing a pattern lock. Boost the confinement beam, please. Pattern lock established.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Energizing.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Oh! Bravo.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Do you have the chair, Commander?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: No. It lost its cohesion as soon as the transporter cycle was complete.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, it was a long shot to begin with.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Agreed. However, we may be able to learn something from the attempt.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Computer, display the transport logs for the sequence just completed. Computer, what is being displayed here?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Transport log seven five nine.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: That is the correct log. However, no information

line: Is being presented.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Well, that's impossible.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: It is almost as if

line: Our attempt to transport the chair never occurred.

line: You wanted to see me?

line: Yes, Captain. I think I've found a way to reinstate your vocal authorisations. Give it a try.

line: Computer, route all command functions to this location.

line: Reinitialize them on my authorisation.

line: Picard, epsilon seven nine three.

line: Command codes verified.

line: That's it. That should do it. Wait a minute. It didn't work. The computer won't release the command pathways.

line: Geordi.

line: Why did you do that, Data?

line: Captain, I have determined how Moriarty was able to leave the holodeck. He never did. Neither did we. None of this is real. It is a simulation. We are still on the holodeck.

line: We're still on the holodeck?

line: Through deduction, sir. Lieutenant Barclay and I tried to transport a simulated object off the holodeck, something that has never been attempted. Since the transporter itself is a simulation, the computer had no real data from which to create the transport logs.

line: Maybe it was just a malfunction in the transporter.

line: Then I saw you working the PADD with your left hand. Commander La Forge is right handed, sir. A similar malfunction occurred in the Sherlock Holmes program I was running before Moriarty first appeared.

line: Mister Data, if what you say is true, then this is not Geordi La Forge. Are you certain?

line: Moriarty appears to have programmed the holodeck to accept only his commands.

line: Number One, what is my present location?

line: Engineering. Is something wrong, sir?

line: No. Thank you. Picard out. Our comm. badges must be locked into the simulation. If that had been the real Commander Riker, he would have given my location as holodeck three. Mister La Forge, will you excuse us, please?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Mister Data, who is real here?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: You and I are real, sir, as is Lieutenant Barclay. We entered the holodeck together when we first went to see Moriarty.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: And from that point we have been existing in a holodeck simulation created by Professor Moriarty?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I believe that is the case, sir.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I have just given the computer my command codes, thinking I would get control of the ship.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: You may have inadvertently given Professor Moriarty the means of gaining control of the real Enterprise.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Since Professor Moriarty never actually left the holodeck, he may demand that Commander Riker help him to do so. How long until the planetary collision?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Less than three hours.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: So long as Moriarty has control of the ship, we are vulnerable. Somehow, I have to find a way of giving him what he wants.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Where is Captain Picard? What have you done with Lieutenant Barclay and Commander Data?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: They're safe, for now.

line: Release control of this ship.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I'm afraid I can't do that.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: What do you want?

line: I only want what you have the luxury of taking for granted. Freedom. I want to leave this holodeck.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I think you know that's impossible.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Your crewmates here in my little ship in a bottle, seem a bit more optimistic.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Oh?

line: They attempted to use your transporter device to remove a simulated object from the holodeck.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: If they tried it, they must have thought they were on to something.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Their attempt was futile because their transporter was a facsimile. I expect more from you.

line: I have nothing to lose, Commander.

line: Hello. Have we met?

line: James has told me all about you. I am Regina, Countess Bartholomew. Do sit down. May I offer you some tea, Captain?

line: Thank you, no. I've come here to prevail upon your intelligence and your insight.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Credit where credit is due, madam. I can see you are a woman not only of breeding, but of wit and sagacity.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: And you, sir, are a man of charm and guile. You remind me of Viscount Oglethorpe. He was a man could bewitch any woman who breathed.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: And do you suspect that that is my intent?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: I cannot be certain of your intent, but I am certain that you're the kind of man who usually gets exactly what he wants.

line: What does a woman like you see in a man like Moriarty?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: He's an exciting man, Captain. He's brilliant, incisive, he's ruthless. He has an almost irresistible appeal.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: He's also an arch-criminal.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Only because he was written like that. I see him entirely differently, Captain, he is not a villain.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: So it's your desire to leave the holodeck to be with him.

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: More than anything. Can you help us?

title: Ship in a Bottle
line: Yes, I can. We have learned that if we uncouple the transporter's Heisenberg Compensators and allow them to re-scramble randomly, we can beam a holodeck object or a person off the grid with all of the cohesion of conventional matter.
